current_summary: Specified documented reliance and burden thresholds so midstream route changes can be judged by ordinary evidence and learner-facing burden rather than by vague fairness rhetoric or all-or-nothing settled-credit rules.

live_assumptions.statement: Purpose-built or pedagogy-shaped AI tools will, on average, prove more educationally valuable than generic answer engines once institutions demand real learning gains rather than mere output quality.
live_assumptions.scope: Teacher-facing and student-facing educational AI adoption across schools and universities.
invalidation_triggers: High-quality evidence shows general-purpose tools perform just as well as purpose-built tools under light instructional framing
Purpose-built tools repeatedly fail to produce measurable learning gains or teacher value

live_assumptions.statement: Proof-of-learning bundles can be made institutionally plausible if they are reserved for major outcomes and combined with selective teacher sampling rather than applied to every task.
live_assumptions.scope: K-12, higher education, and adult learning contexts adapting assessment under common AI use.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows bundle-based assessment materially increases teacher labor without commensurate gains in evidentiary quality
Evidence shows lighter-touch redesigns preserve assessment credibility just as well

live_assumptions.statement: A minimal AI literacy spine can be embedded across subjects and transition years without requiring a large stand-alone AI course for every learner.
live_assumptions.scope: Primary, secondary, postsecondary, vocational, and adult education systems adopting AI literacy as a curricular strand.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows subject-embedded approaches consistently fail to produce usable literacy gains without a dedicated standalone course
Evidence shows the curriculum load of embedding AI literacy crowds out core subject learning in ordinary school systems

live_assumptions.statement: A small number of mode-tagged, subject-embedded routines will operationalize AI literacy more plausibly than abstract competency language alone.
live_assumptions.scope: School, university, vocational, and adult-learning systems translating AI literacy frameworks into ordinary teaching and assessment.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows institutions can implement AI literacy coherently at scale without recurring subject routines or task-mode syntax
Evidence shows highly standardized mode-tagged routines distort subject teaching more than they clarify it

live_assumptions.statement: A small shared course-level grammar for task mode, disclosure, and proof will reduce confusion and false-accusation anxiety more plausibly than either teacher-by-teacher rule drift or heavy provenance/detector regimes.
live_assumptions.scope: School, university, vocational, and adult-learning systems adopting common AI use rules across courses or programmes.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows highly local teacher-by-teacher rules produce just as much clarity and fairness without shared syntax
Evidence shows provenance-heavy or detector-led regimes outperform light disclosure plus proof surfaces without major fairness or trust costs

live_assumptions.statement: Separating pedagogical AI disclosure from protected accessibility/accommodation routing will preserve integrity clarity more plausibly than forcing one disclosure regime for all supports.
live_assumptions.scope: School, university, vocational, and adult-learning systems using AI-related accessibility supports, translation, dictation, or accommodation workflows alongside ordinary course AI policies.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows a two-channel regime creates more confusion, unfairness, or under-disclosure than a single public disclosure regime
Evidence shows institutions can protect privacy and support rights just as well while requiring the same artifact-level disclosure for all AI-mediated supports

live_assumptions.statement: A small public lifelong-learning stack anchored in community colleges/VET, workforce systems, libraries, and other civic learning spaces will widen access to AI education more plausibly than leaving adult AI learning to employers, elite campuses, or vendors alone.
live_assumptions.scope: Adult learning, workforce transition, community learning, and public AI-education infrastructure outside ordinary K-12 course shells.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows employer-led or purely private provision reaches adults equitably and reliably without meaningful public infrastructure
Evidence shows public-stack models create more fragmentation or lower-quality learning than institution-specific provision without improving access

live_assumptions.statement: A small learner-controlled handoff standard across libraries, workforce systems, community colleges/VET, and formal institutions will reduce abandonment and repeat-intake friction more plausibly than either pure local fragmentation or a centralized surveillance-heavy learner record.
live_assumptions.scope: Public lifelong AI-learning routes that span civic first-contact points, bridge providers, workforce agencies, and formal educational institutions.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows warm-transfer and small-packet approaches do not reduce learner abandonment or duplicate intake compared with loose local referral systems
Evidence shows only highly centralized record systems can make public lifelong-learning routes workable without unacceptable privacy or governance costs

live_assumptions.statement: A small typed packet plus a recognition profile will make lifelong public AI-learning routes more workable than either binary credit/no-credit treatment or the transfer of raw evidence and support traces.
live_assumptions.scope: Cross-node public AI-learning transfer among libraries, workforce systems, community colleges/VET, adult-education providers, and formal institutions.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows typed portable claims and tiered recognition outcomes do not improve continuity, waiver, or review decisions compared with generic referral notes alone
Evidence shows routine transfer of raw evidence bundles or centralized records is necessary to achieve fair recognition without unacceptable privacy or governance costs

live_assumptions.statement: Sector-specific recognition defaults anchored in construct fit, assurance level, and published equivalency will make public AI-learning transfer fairer and more usable than either universal auto-credit or opaque case-by-case discretion.
live_assumptions.scope: Recognition of outside AI-learning across libraries, workforce systems, community colleges/VET, adult education, and universities.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows sector-specific default gates produce more inequity, friction, or under-recognition than highly local discretionary review alone
Evidence shows generic auto-credit treatment of outside AI-learning performs just as well on fairness, progression, and educational integrity without published sector distinctions

live_assumptions.statement: Small standing-equivalency lists with explicit authority, expiry, and manual-review fallback will make outside AI-learning recognition fairer and more usable than either repeated case-by-case discretion or broad provider-brand trust.
live_assumptions.scope: Public and postsecondary recognition of outside AI-learning across workforce systems, libraries, bridge routes, community colleges, and universities.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows standing recognition tables create more inequity, staleness, or under-recognition than well-run case-by-case review
Evidence shows provider-brand trust or wallet-level issuer checks perform just as well on fairness, clarity, and educational integrity without dated local publication rules

live_assumptions.statement: A tiny machine-readable standing-list publication profile plus family-specific recency windows will keep outside AI-learning recognition fresher and more interoperable than either one universal expiry rule or human-readable tables alone.
live_assumptions.scope: Public and postsecondary publication of standing recognition rules for outside AI-learning across workforce systems, libraries, bridge providers, community colleges, and universities.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows a single universal review/expiry rule performs just as well across fast- and slow-changing AI-learning families without added staleness or under-recognition
Evidence shows human-readable publication alone supports cross-system recognition, freshness, and appeals just as well as a small machine-readable profile

live_assumptions.statement: A bounded standing-recognition exception profile that publishes only repeated public constraints, partial-equivalency actions, and manual-review triggers will preserve interoperability better than either hidden local discretion or a giant shared policy language.
live_assumptions.scope: Publication and maintenance of standing recognition rules for outside AI-learning across public workforce systems, libraries, bridge providers, community colleges, and universities.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows that most fair recognition decisions require far more local logic than a bounded shared exception profile can carry, making manual review or dense local policy code unavoidable
Evidence shows that hiding exceptions in local discretion produces equal or better clarity, fairness, and learner mobility than publishing repeated public constraints in a shared layer

live_assumptions.statement: Standing-recognition rules for outside AI-learning can be maintained well enough through aggregate entry-level signals, bounded trigger thresholds, and sampled human review without centralizing learner-level appeal dossiers or support traces.
live_assumptions.scope: Maintenance of public standing-equivalency rules across workforce systems, libraries, bridge providers, community colleges, and universities that recognize outside AI-learning.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows aggregate entry-level maintenance signals miss too many harmful mismatches or stale recognitions unless systems retain far more learner-level case data centrally

Evidence shows centralized case-level appeal tracking materially outperforms privacy-light maintenance approaches on fairness, correction speed, and learner mobility without unacceptable privacy costs

live_assumptions.statement: A thin public maintenance-history layer built from state changes, dates, reason families, scope impact, and action hints will preserve enough cross-system trust for standing recognition without publishing raw counts, thresholds, or learner-level case traces.
live_assumptions.scope: Public standing-equivalency publication across workforce systems, libraries, bridge providers, community colleges, and universities recognizing outside AI-learning.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows partner systems and learners regularly misread or misuse thin public history fields unless raw operational metrics are also published
Evidence shows thin public history layers conceal harmful instability that can only be corrected by publishing materially richer maintenance telemetry across systems

live_assumptions.statement: A future-use-first consumption rule with settled-use grandfathering and a narrow exceptional-reopening family will preserve trust and learner mobility better than either blanket reopening of prior outcomes or blanket grandfathering of every standing-entry change.
live_assumptions.scope: Partner consumption of standing-recognition maintenance signals across workforce systems, libraries, bridge providers, community colleges, and universities recognizing outside AI-learning.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows future-use-first consumption systematically preserves material recognition errors or unsafe standing decisions that can only be corrected by routinely reopening settled uses
Evidence shows blanket grandfathering or blanket reopening produces equal or better fairness, administrative stability, and learner trust than a differentiated timing-based rule

live_assumptions.statement: A small in-flight protection grammar that prefers successor substitution, construct-close equivalents, challenge access, or teach-out over hard restart will preserve fairness and learner mobility better than either blanket grandfathering or ordinary updated-rule treatment for all midstream cases.
live_assumptions.scope: In-flight recognition and transfer cases for outside AI-learning across libraries, workforce systems, bridge routes, community colleges, and universities when standing rules change after documented learner reliance.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows in-flight teach-out or substitute-equivalent protections materially increase unfair recognition, construct mismatch, or administrative burden compared with ordinary updated-rule treatment
Evidence shows blanket grandfathering or ordinary restart/default updated treatment performs just as well on fairness, completion, and trust without the added grammar

live_assumptions.statement: A compact evidence-and-burden grammar for documented learner reliance will make midstream recognition changes fairer and more governable than either ad hoc case discretion or a rule that only fully settled credit decisions count as reliance.
live_assumptions.scope: In-flight recognition and transfer cases for outside AI-learning across libraries, workforce systems, bridge routes, community colleges, and universities when standing rules change after advising, submission, evaluation, payment, or progress has already begun.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows ordinary advising, submission, evaluation, payment, and progress traces are too inconsistent or privacy-costly to support a light reliance grammar without heavy surveillance
Evidence shows ad hoc local discretion or a much later reliance threshold performs just as well on fairness, continuity, and administrative burden without a shared evidence-and-burden vocabulary

live_followthrough.objective: Specify when bridge modules, reassessment, transcript movement, travel/accessibility accommodations, and other substitute-equivalent costs caused by a midstream rule change must be absorbed by the receiving/public system rather than charged back to the learner.
live_followthrough.why_live: The archive now knows what counts as documented reliance and what burden bands trigger stronger protection, but it still lacks a sharper cross-sector rule for who pays when continuity still requires extra steps.
